items.title: The cokernel of the last differential of a flat complex with bounded tor amplitude is flat

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a bounded above complex of flat modules with tor amplitude in [a, b], the cokernel of the differential d^{a-1} is again flat (statement lines 12402-12409). The proof has to align the degree bookkeeping: flatness of the terms makes the ordinary tensor product compute the derived one, the tor amplitude hypothesis is used in degree a - 1 to get middle exactness of E^{a-2} tensor F -> E^{a-1} tensor F -> E^a tensor F for every test module F, and the truncated complex E^{a-2} -> E^{a-1} -> E^a -> Coker(d^{a-1}) -> 0 is recognised as a flat resolution, which identifies that middle exactness with the vanishing of Tor_1 of the cokernel (proof lines 12412-12427). The final step is the same-chapter Tor criterion for flatness. The claim is H2: one degree-shifted bookkeeping argument, all inside the counted span.
